selection_reasoning: These three tasks form a coherent exploration-and-progression chain inside a custom structure. The player must first mine through an oak_slab barrier (e.g., a floor/ceiling block) to gain access to a room containing glass blocks. Beyond or within that glass-walled area, purple stained glass is placed in a deeper chamber. Each task gates the next: mining the slab opens the path, finding glass confirms the player is in the right area, and finding purple stained glass is the final objective in a connected but distinct location. All tasks are observable, verifiable, and require no deep Minecraft crafting knowledge.

edges.reason: Mining the oak_slab barrier opens access to the glass-walled room behind it; glass is not visible or reachable until the slab is removed.
The glass room contains a passage leading to a deeper chamber with purple_stained_glass; the player must navigate through the glass area first.

milestones.description: Uses inventory_has because mining oak slabs (including double oak slabs) drops oak_slab items into the player's inventory. The player must break at least one oak slab from the double-slab barrier blocking the entrance. Double oak slabs drop 2 oak slabs when mined, so min_count=1 is easily satisfied. This is the preferred rule type for mine tasks since the mined drop ends up in inventory.

Uses position_near_with_facing because 'find glass' is an observation/locate task — the player must navigate near the glass walls and be facing them. The target (5, 1, 7) is the center of the glass corridor (z=6-8). max_distance=3 ensures the player has actually entered the corridor (they must be past z=4, meaning they've mined through the oak slab barrier). facing_tolerance=60 ensures they are looking toward the glass walls. This is preferred over position_inside_box because it correctly models 'player can see the glass blocks'.

Uses position_near_with_facing because 'find purple_stained_glass' is an observation/locate task — the player must navigate deeper into the structure to the purple stained glass chamber and face it. The target (5, 1, 10) is the center of the purple stained glass chamber (z=9-11). max_distance=3 ensures the player has actually reached the purple chamber area (they must be past z=7, meaning they've traversed the glass corridor). facing_tolerance=60 ensures they are looking toward the purple stained glass. This is preferred over position_inside_box because it correctly models visual observation of the target blocks.

scene_description: A stone brick building with a sealed entrance blocked by double oak slabs. Behind the barrier is a stone brick antechamber, then a glass-walled corridor, and finally a purple stained glass inner chamber. The player must mine through the oak slab barrier to access the glass corridor, then proceed deeper to find the purple stained glass chamber.
task_text: Mine through the oak slab barrier blocking the building entrance using your wooden axe. Once inside, find the glass corridor, then continue deeper to find the purple stained glass chamber.
design_notes: Structure at z=3-12, x=3-8. Double oak slabs at z=3 (front) and z=4 (inner) create a 2-deep fully opaque barrier at x=5-6, y=0-2. Stone bricks fill the rest of the front wall and the z=4-5 antechamber walls. Glass corridor at z=6-8 with 2-wide air passage. Purple stained glass chamber at z=9-11 with 2-wide air passage. Player spawns at (5,0,0) facing south (180°, pitch 5°) with wooden axe. The double slabs render as full blocks — completely opaque, no visibility through to interior.
